headline: Opening night, bleachers still under construction.
The Cup, lifted at home.
note: First time since 1938 they won it on home ice. Dana cried at the anthem, I cried at the horn.

headline: First postseason clincher at Wrigley. Ever.
note: Champagne on the field at Wrigley. I didn't know that was allowed.

headline: The pennant, finally.
note: They played Go Cubs Go and an entire neighborhood sang it on the walk home.

headline: First World Series game at Wrigley since 1945.
Down 3–1. Still alive.
note: Dad waited 71 years for this and I waited 35. When the last out landed in Rizzo's glove he grabbed my arm so hard it bruised. Nobody left. Nobody wanted to.

plays.text: Ramírez lines a solo home run to left. Cleveland leads.
Bryant crushes a solo shot to left-center. Tie game.
Russell beats out an infield single. Chicago takes the lead.
Lindor singles home a run after a stolen base. 3–2.
Chapman enters with one out in the seventh. Eight outs to go.
Ramírez grounds out. Chicago lives. Series heads back to Cleveland.

headline: 4–0 at 25 minutes. 4–4 at the whistle.
note: The Yellow Wall was singing at 4–0 and still singing at 4–4. I don't speak German and I knew every word by the end.

headline: A rivalry in October, from the Monster seats.
Fifteen points. Six allowed. Pure defense.
The double doink.
note: Forty-one yards. The upright, the crossbar, the grass. 62,000 people went silent at once. I've never heard a sound like that silence.

headline: Four goals from one man, ten rows from the pitch.
note: Leo counted every goal out loud in Spanish. Cinco.

headline: The last game before the world went quiet.
note: We didn't know it yet, but this was the last crowd any of us would stand in for a year and a half.

headline: Turn 1 from the hill, with 140,000 others.

plays.text: Hamilton takes the lead into Turn 1.
Verstappen passes after the final stops.

headline: 62,000 came for one player. He didn't play.
The kick that went through the snow.
note: Maya's first time at Lambeau. Leo wore three pairs of socks and still complained. When the kick went up nobody in our row breathed, and then the whole visitors' corner lost it. We drove home through the snow singing.

plays.text: Touchdown, Chicago. A quiet road crowd suddenly isn't.
Touchdown, Chicago, just before the half.
Touchdown, Chicago. 21–7 and the visitors' corner is loud.
Touchdown and two-point try good. Green Bay leads 22–21.
51-yard field goal as time expires. Chicago wins it.
